clue.text: Inexperienced retailers — those selling fruit and veg

parts.note: a green beginner is new and untried
grocers are shopkeepers who sell food

explanation.surface: A dig at shopkeepers new to the trade, the ones running fruit and vegetable stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads almost literally: the wordplay half and the definition half describe the same people.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengrocer is the British name for a shopkeeper whose stock is fresh produce such as apples and cabbages.

clue.text: They can improve people's looks

parts.note: surface reading: something like make-up or a good haircut that makes people more attractive
setter's reading: looks means the act of looking, so these things improve eyesight

explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites thoughts of cosmetics; 'looks' really means how well people see.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles worn on the face correct poor vision, sharpening what wearers see when they look.

clue.text: Issue the man at "Exeter News" keeps hidden

indicators.note: something kept hidden is tucked inside the run of words, so the answer sits concealed in them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the, all of man and at, and the start of Exeter
surface padding: it completes the newspaper title but supplies no letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper in Devon is suppressing a story from one of its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News' only completes the newspaper picture; the letters come from the words before it. Exeter is a city in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue, as a verb, is to come out or flow forth from a source, which is what emanating means.

clue.text: Gossiping at ten, possibly on telephone

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it is written above it, so it comes first
possibly suggests the words could take another form, so their letters may be rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange
to ring someone is to telephone them

explanation.surface: Someone spends the evening chatting idly on the phone from ten o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is informal British for chatting at length about trivial things, much like gossiping.

clue.text: Get to deliver a sermon, but not first

indicators.note: not first tells the solver to drop the opening letter of the word clued

parts.note: a priest giving a sermon is preaching

explanation.surface: A vicar finally gets the chance to give a sermon, though not as the first speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to' reads like 'have the opportunity to', but it is the definition: arrive at.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to a place is to arrive there, the same as reaching a destination.

clue.text: Players, shown the way, made a chess move

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast
someone shown the way has been led

explanation.surface: Actors are guided to a chessboard and make a move in a staged game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests chess players, but it means actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is a special chess manoeuvre moving king and rook together in a single turn.

clue.text: Going round at great yachting event

indicators.note: letters going round are turned about and shuffled into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Boats circle the course at high speed during a sailing competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, typically sailing or rowing, held as a sporting occasion.

clue.text: Sharp chord is specially written for stringed instruments

indicators.note: something specially written is composed afresh, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: the three words supply all twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A composer pens a particular sharp chord for a group of instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'sharp chord' look like notation, but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpsichord is a keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked by quills, so it counts among stringed instruments.

clue.text: In Canada man tries very hard

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow, running across their boundaries

parts.note: the letters span the end of Canada, all of man and the start of tries

explanation.surface: A Canadian man makes a strenuous effort at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tries very hard' reads as one phrase, but 'tries' gives letters and 'very hard' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone unyielding and firm, and originally a legendary stone of supreme hardness.

clue.text: Appoints fool to hold placard

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
a placard is a sign held up at a protest

explanation.surface: A buffoon is chosen to carry the banner at a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign someone is to designate them for a task or post, the same as appointing them.

clue.text: Giving up and showing the white flag?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: yielding or handing something over
second meaning: what an army does to signal it will stop fighting

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second half is a picture rather than a dictionary phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving a white flag is the traditional battlefield signal of capitulation, and capitulating is ceasing resistance.

clue.text: Spend time on part of the Bible

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone devotes hours to studying a section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is an extract or section of a written text, such as a few verses from scripture.

clue.text: One carrying a weapon?

parts.note: surface reading: an armed person, such as a gunman or soldier
setter's reading: an object that literally holds a pistol on the belt

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to an armed person; the answer is the leather case on the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a sheath worn at the waist or shoulder in which a handgun is kept.

clue.text: The subject being discussed is a girl

parts.note: taken as written
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The topic of conversation turns out to be a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The issue is the matter or topic under debate, the point people are arguing about.

clue.text: I'm to act as middleman at once

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a go-between who brings two sides together mediates

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are about to step in as a go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate describes something happening without delay, instantly, right now.

clue.text: Unique game gets shorter

parts.note: a match is a game between opponents
less means smaller in amount or extent

explanation.surface: A one-off sporting contest has its playing time cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something matchless has no equal or rival, so it stands alone as one of a kind.

clue.text: Control of little weight for part of car

parts.note: to head something is to lead or be in charge of it
something light weighs little

explanation.surface: Handling a lightweight component of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Headlights are the lamps on the front of a vehicle that illuminate the road at night.

clue.text: Potent liqueur mixed in baths

indicators.note: mixed suggests ingredients stirred together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Strong spirits are being blended in a bathtub, like bootleg gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong green aniseed spirit flavoured with wormwood, famously high in alcohol.

clue.text: Ridicule the French politician with nothing on

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
MP is a Member of Parliament
the figure zero looks like the letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mocking a French politician who appears with no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to mock them publicly through satire or caricature.

clue.text: Money for food

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the baked loaf, a staple of eating

explanation.surface: Cash spent on groceries.
explanation.definitionFit: The baked staple made from flour is also a slang term for cash, as in earning a living.

clue.text: Boasting it's almost brave to fuss

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
ado is fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A comment that making a song and dance about something takes nearly as much courage as bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy display of boldness meant to impress, a form of swaggering talk.

clue.text: Smile — it could lead to pride in chosen group

indicators.note: the letters could be reworked to produce something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A smug smile hints at the conceit of belonging to an exclusive club.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief that a select few are superior, and the snobbish pride that goes with it.

clue.text: Putting an amount in a pipe started again

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, with in marking where it goes

parts.note: a reed is a simple pipe, as in a wind instrument
a sum is an amount, especially of money

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs money into a tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to carry on after a pause, so something resumed has started again.

clue.text: Thick part of wooden seat

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a portion of the following words

parts.note: the letters span the end of wooden and the start of seat

explanation.surface: A sturdy chunk of a timber bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means thick in the sense of closely packed, and also slow-witted.

clue.text: Hair Eve dealt with, having more weight

indicators.note: something dealt with has been worked on and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Eve has her hair done and it ends up bulkier than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavier is the comparative of heavy, describing something that weighs more.

clue.text: Said son gets depressed after nightfall

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the next word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: the star in our sky is pronounced the same as a male child
someone down is low in spirits

explanation.surface: A boy grows gloomy once evening comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after nightfall' reads as a time phrase; 'after' only joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundown is the time when the sun sets, when daylight ends and evening begins.

clue.text: Relative being beheaded causes high spirits

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: a relation is a family member

explanation.surface: A family member's execution oddly makes someone cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness and exhilaration, a state of joy.

clue.text: During which there could be a lightning strike?

definitions.text: During which there could be a lightning strike?

parts.words: During which there could be a lightning strike?
parts.note: surface reading: an industrial dispute, a sudden walkout by workers
setter's reading: a bolt of electricity from the sky hitting the ground

explanation.walkthrough: A lightning strike is a British term for a sudden walkout by workers without notice; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather event with heavy rain, rumbling noise and flashes of electricity is when bolts hit the ground.
